text.text: Every procedure has an owner, an approver and a next review date. Filter by department, check what is overdue and ask people to sign off once approved.
State the purpose in one sentence.
List who it applies to and who is responsible.
Write numbered steps. One action per step.
Add a checklist for anything that must not be missed.
Say what to do when it goes wrong.
Record the version and a short change note.
If a new hire cannot follow it without asking questions, it is not finished.

Weak: "Check the equipment before leaving." Strong: "Open the van, scan the tool tag, and tick each tool against the list. If a tool is missing, do not leave; message dispatch with the tag number." The strong version has an action, a tool and a stop rule.
Give every SOP one owner and one approver; they may not be the same person.
Set the next review date when you approve it, not later.
Ask the first new person who follows it to mark anything unclear.
Reading the procedure aloud with the person who does the work finds more problems than any amount of silent proofreading.
Open the review calendar and list what is due
Read each SOP aloud with its owner
Bump the version and reset the next review date
Ask the team to sign off again
Open the Review overdue view. It should be empty. If something is still there, give it a date and an owner before everyone leaves the room.
